module_title: Co-extensive Liability, Duties of Bailee, and Creation of Agency
introduction: This intermediate tier explores the operational mechanics of these contracts. It details the extent of a Surety's liability, the legal position of a Finder of Goods, and how an Agency relationship can be created implicitly or explicitly.

core_concepts.title: Surety's Liability is Co-extensive (Section 128)
core_concepts.description:
Unless otherwise provided in the contract, the liability of the surety is co-extensive with that of the principal debtor.
- Application: If the debtor owes 1 Lakh + 10% interest, the surety is liable for the exact same amount. The creditor can sue the surety *directly* without suing the principal debtor first (unless the contract states otherwise).

core_concepts.title: Continuing Guarantee (Section 129)
core_concepts.description:
A guarantee which extends to a series of transactions (not just a single debt).
- Revocation (Sec 130): It can be revoked by the surety at any time regarding *future transactions* by giving notice to the creditor.
- Death of Surety (Sec 131): Automatically revokes a continuing guarantee regarding future transactions.

core_concepts.title: Finder of Lost Goods (Section 71 & 168)
core_concepts.description:
A person who finds goods belonging to another and takes them into custody is subject to the same responsibility as a **Bailee**.
- Right of Lien: The finder can retain the goods until they receive lawful compensation for the trouble and expense incurred in finding the owner, but they cannot sue the owner for such compensation (unless a specific reward was offered).

core_concepts.title: Creation of Agency
core_concepts.description:
No consideration is necessary to create an agency (Sec 185). An agency can be created:
1. Expressly: By spoken or written words (e.g., Power of Attorney).
2. Impliedly: By conduct or circumstances.
3. By Necessity: Selling perishable goods belonging to the principal to prevent total loss.
4. By Ratification (Sec 196): When an agent acts without authority, but the principal later approves and adopts the act, the agency is established retrospectively.

important_entities.name: Standard of Care by Bailee (Section 151)
important_entities.key_fact: A Bailee must take reasonable care of the goods.
important_entities.significance: A bailee is bound to take as much care of the goods bailed to them as a man of ordinary prudence would take of his own goods under similar circumstances. If they take such care, they are NOT responsible for the loss or destruction of the goods (Sec 152).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: In a Contract of Indemnity, the liability of the indemnifier is **Primary** and independent. In a Contract of Guarantee, the liability of the surety is **Secondary** (it only arises IF the principal debtor defaults).

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: E I N R (Express, Implied, Necessity, Ratification)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember the 4 ways an agency can be legally established.

exam_strategy_tips: If a Judiciary exam asks 'Does the Creditor have to exhaust all remedies against the Principal Debtor before suing the Surety?', the answer is **NO**. The Surety's liability is co-extensive and immediate upon default (Sec 128).
